title: Transdimensional quantum droplets in an optically trapped Bose mixture
authors: Xiaoran Ye, Yi Zhang, Ziheng Zhou, Zhaoxin Liang
abstract: We study quantum droplets in a symmetric two-component Bose mixture with interspecies $p$-wave interactions and a two-dimensional transverse optical lattice. The lattice drives a crossover from an anisotropic three-dimensional gas to weakly coupled one-dimensional tubes. We calculate the ground-state energy and quantum depletion at the Gaussian level and derive their limiting forms. At $y=g_{12}/g=-0.95$, where the bare mean field is repulsive and no free-space droplet exists, the calculated bulk equation of state supports a self-bound minimum across the crossover: a negative lattice contribution at order $n^{2}$ supplies the attraction in the three-dimensional regime, and attractive fluctuations do so in the quasi-one-dimensional regime, with the intermediate, transdimensional range described quantitatively by neither limit. The interspecies $p$-wave interaction modifies only the spin branch. In the parameter range studied, increasing its strength lowers the equilibrium density across the crossover, consistently with a weakening of the induced binding.
summary: This paper theoretically examines quantum droplets in a two-component Bose mixture confined by an optical lattice, analyzing the crossover from 3D to quasi-1D regimes. Using functional-integral methods, the authors show that the self-binding mechanism persists across this crossover, with the attraction sourced differently in the 3D versus 1D limits. The results quantify the influence of p-wave interactions on this induced binding.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum droplets in a symmetric two-component Bose mixture confined by an optical lattice, specifically focusing on the crossover between different dimensional regimes.
main_result: The system supports a self-bound minimum across the dimensional crossover, with the attraction arising from different physical mechanisms (lattice vs. fluctuations) depending on the regime.
method: The analysis employs the Euclidean functional-integral framework, calculating observables like ground-state energy and quantum depletion at the Gaussian level.
model_or_system: The system is a two-component Bose mixture ($\psi_1, \psi_2$) subjected to a 2D transverse optical lattice, incorporating s-wave and p-wave interspecies interactions.
key_observables: Ground-state energy, quantum depletion, and the equilibrium density across the dimensional crossover.
important_parameters: Lattice depths ($t_1, t_2$), interspecies coupling ratio ($y = g_{12}/g$), and p-wave interaction strength ($g_p$).
main_assumptions: Assumes equal masses and intraspecies couplings, and uses the lowest-band approximation for the lattice confinement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice structure and the crossover from 3D to quasi-1D regimes, and show the energy per particle versus density, confirming the existence of a finite-density minimum.
paper_structure: The paper builds from deriving the Euclidean action in the tight-binding regime, calculating the ground-state energy and quantum depletion via Gaussian fluctuations, and finally analyzing the resulting equation of state across the dimensional crossover.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how dimensionality and specific interspecies interactions (p-wave) govern the stability and binding mechanism of quantum droplets in engineered optical lattices.
